:::{#sol-best-predictor}

1. For each value of $\Predvar$, compute the conditional expectation:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar = 0}
   &= 0 \cd 0.5 + 2 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 1
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar = 1}
   &= 4 \cd 0.5 + 6 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 5
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   By the law of iterated expectations (@thm-lie), the marginal mean is:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\Outvar}
   &= \E{\E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}} \\
   &= 1 \cd 0.5 + 5 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 3
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   The conditional expectation function is $\bestpredfnf{0} = 1$ and $\bestpredfnf{1} = 5$,
   which can also be written $\bestpredfnf{\Predvar} = 1 + 4\Predvar$.

2. For the constant prediction $\predfn_1\paren{\Predvar} = 3$:
   Given $\Predvar = 0$:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\sqf{\Outvar - 3} \mid \Predvar = 0}
   &= \sqf{0 - 3} \cd 0.5 + \sqf{2 - 3} \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 9 \cd 0.5 + 1 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 5
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   Given $\Predvar = 1$:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\sqf{\Outvar - 3} \mid \Predvar = 1}
   &= \sqf{4 - 3} \cd 0.5 + \sqf{6 - 3} \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 1 \cd 0.5 + 9 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 5
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   By the law of iterated expectations (@thm-lie):
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\sqf{\Outvar - \predfn_1\paren{\Predvar}}}
   &= \E{\E{\sqf{\Outvar - 3} \mid \Predvar}} \\
   &= 5 \cd 0.5 + 5 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 5
   \end{aligned}
   $$

3. For the prediction $\predfn_2\paren{\Predvar} = 4\Predvar$:
   Here $\predfn_2\paren{0} = 0$ and $\predfn_2\paren{1} = 4$.
   Given $\Predvar = 0$:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\sqf{\Outvar - 0} \mid \Predvar = 0}
   &= \sqf{0 - 0} \cd 0.5 + \sqf{2 - 0} \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 0 \cd 0.5 + 4 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 2
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   Given $\Predvar = 1$:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\sqf{\Outvar - 4} \mid \Predvar = 1}
   &= \sqf{4 - 4} \cd 0.5 + \sqf{6 - 4} \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 0 \cd 0.5 + 4 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 2
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   By @thm-lie:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\sqf{\Outvar - \predfn_2\paren{\Predvar}}}
   &= 2 \cd 0.5 + 2 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 2
   \end{aligned}
   $$

4. For the conditional mean predictor $\bestpredfnf{\Predvar} = \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}$:
   Given $\Predvar = 0$, $\bestpredfnf{0} = 1$:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\sqf{\Outvar - 1} \mid \Predvar = 0}
   &= \sqf{0 - 1} \cd 0.5 + \sqf{2 - 1} \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 1 \cd 0.5 + 1 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 1
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   Given $\Predvar = 1$, $\bestpredfnf{1} = 5$:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\sqf{\Outvar - 5} \mid \Predvar = 1}
   &= \sqf{4 - 5} \cd 0.5 + \sqf{6 - 5} \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 1 \cd 0.5 + 1 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 1
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   By @thm-lie:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \E{\sqf{\Outvar - \bestpredfnf{\Predvar}}}
   &= 1 \cd 0.5 + 1 \cd 0.5 \\
   &= 1
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   The conditional mean predictor $\bestpredfn$ achieves the lowest risk ($1$),
   strictly outperforming $\predfn_2$ ($2$) and the constant prediction $\predfn_1$ ($5$).

:::
